findings: ALK21-006EXT was a nonrandomized, open-label extension of base study NCT01218997; all 108 enrolled participants used monthly VIVITROL 380 mg after prior naltrexone exposure.
Alkermes terminated this safety-focused extension for business reasons in December 2006, not because a controlled primary efficacy endpoint failed.
Registry reports median treatment duration 43 weeks; primary endpoint was treatment-emergent adverse-event incidence over up to three years.
records.limitations: Source is official registry design/disposition summary but not a downloaded full protocol/SAP document.

findings: Registry NCT01218958 is Alkermes ALK21-003, covering February 2002 through September 2003, 190 mg/380 mg monthly extended-release naltrexone and placebo.
Garbutt et al. 2005 randomized 627 actively drinking adults at 24 US sites to 380 mg, 190 mg or placebo plus psychosocial counselling, assessing heavy-drinking event rate.
JAMA study reported 25% heavy-drinking event-rate reduction at 380 mg versus placebo, P=0.02 (corrected), while 190 mg was nonsignificant P=0.07; subgroup effects varied by sex and prior abstinence.
The 2005 paper predates ClinicalTrials.gov posting of the ALK21-003 record; linkage is supported by sponsor study code, dates, arms and sample, not an NCT citation in the paper.
records.limitations: Early publication predates retrospective registry posting. Require protocol version and outcome-definition reconciliation before treating analyses as prospectively prespecified against a dated registration.

findings: Original 52-week international Phase 3 open-label safety study of aripiprazole lauroxil NCT01626456 included both former participants in pivotal NCT01469039 and de novo patients who switched from oral antipsychotics.
Reported treatment-emergent adverse events 50.4%, insomnia 8.4%, weight increased 5.0%, akathisia 3.8% and other extrapyramidal symptoms 9.4%.
An exact-NCT peer-reviewed article describes methods, safety population and tolerability even though full protocol and SAP are not attached to stored registry record.
records.limitations: Nonrandomized extension/open-label study. Group-level percentages and published post hoc symptom trajectories are not a blinded efficacy demonstration.

records.drug: oral naltrexone and buprenorphine transition regimen to extended-release naltrexone
findings: A later post-hoc paper explicitly identifies the NCT02537574 original Phase 3 randomized trial as enrolling 378 participants with untreated opioid use disorder for one-week induction to extended-release naltrexone.
Withdrawal timing was compared after the fact against a distinct stable-buprenorphine population trial NCT02696434 (N=101).
The secondary analysis sheds light on opioid withdrawal and comparability but is not the original randomized primary efficacy contrast or a complete sponsor protocol.
records.limitations: Cross-trial withdrawal patterns can be confounded by entry population. Do not infer the failed original endpoint was met.

findings: Lancet randomized double-blind placebo-controlled 24-week study across 13 Russian sites after inpatient detoxification; 126 assigned extended-release naltrexone 380 mg and 124 placebo.
Patients received counselling; primary confirmed abstinence profile weeks 5 through 24 used urine tests and self-report, analyzed by intention to treat.
Reported median confirmed abstinent weeks 90.0% (XR-NTX) versus 35.0% placebo, P=0.0002, and longer reported retention.
records.limitations: Publication documents methods but is not a full archived sponsor SAP. Trial is historic; result cannot serve as a prospective prediction.

findings: FDA reviewed sponsor ALK9072-003 (NCT01469039) and confirmed both aripiprazole lauroxil doses 441 mg and 882 mg were statistically superior to placebo on PANSS change to Day 85.

Study randomized 1:1:1 to aripiprazole lauroxil 441 mg, 882 mg or IM placebo; active groups also received blinded oral aripiprazole for the first 21 days whereas placebo received matching oral placebo.

Primary ANCOVA used last-observation-carried-forward (LOCF) with study region, treatment and baseline PANSS. FDA identified the 42.1% dropout as a concern with LOCF, requested MMRM and alternative missingness sensitivity analyses; observed-case MMRM still showed both treatments significant at p<0.001.

An unblinded sample-size re-estimation at 271 participants used Cui-Hung-Wang combination with Hommel type-I-error control. FDA says final SAP was submitted before unblinding and unblinding occurred after 2014-03-31 database lock.
These are publicly documented contents of a regulatory statistical review, not the attached original complete SAP document.
records.limitations: Historic 2015 FDA assessment and design-specific missingness caveat; no current Phase 3 forecast; oral lead-in complicates attribution of early efficacy exclusively to injectable formulation.

findings: A long-term extension of NCT01626456 (NCT01895452) followed patients on aripiprazole lauroxil over 180 weeks/3.5 years; published paper explicitly cross-identifies both NCTs.
Published AE frequency across extended follow-up 57.5% overall, EPS-related events 12.8%; exploratory symptom stability/improvement through week 124 reported in a selected subset.
Analysis is useful for durability and tolerability context, not a placebo-controlled maintenance-efficacy effect.
records.limitations: Selected long-term completers are subject to attrition/selection; source is not complete original full protocol or SAP.

findings: FORWARD-5 used randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled sequential parallel-comparison design at 57 sites, compared two BUP/SAM dosages with placebo alongside ongoing antidepressant therapy.
Publication reported primary endpoint success for 2 mg/2 mg: average MADRS-6 change difference -1.5 (P=0.018) and MADRS-10 change difference -1.9 (P=0.026).
FORWARD-4 and FORWARD-5 share core design but are separate trials; FORWARD-4 missed its original endpoint.
records.limitations: Primary comparison data are published; full standalone protocol and SAP attachment are not in stored registry snapshot. Do not interpret one positive trial as proof all program trials succeeded.

findings: FORWARD-4 used sequential parallel-comparison design, randomization, double blinding and placebo control at 54 sites; adjunctive buprenorphine/samidorphan plus continuing antidepressant therapy.
Primary MADRS-10 change at Week 5 did not meet significance: least-squares mean difference -1.8, 95% CI -4.1 to 0.4, P=0.109.
Later exploratory or post-hoc significant EOT measures must not be substituted for the original primary comparison.
records.limitations: Peer-reviewed paper is not a complete original protocol or full SAP attachment; other outcomes should be examined for multiplicity and selection effects.

findings: FORWARD-3 used a double-blind placebo run-in and then six-week randomized adjunctive BUP/SAM 2 mg/2 mg versus placebo for nonresponders at 58 study sites (49 in US, nine in Bulgaria).
Original MADRS-10 primary analysis showed mean change -4.8 vs -4.6 (difference -0.3, P=0.782), not meeting its primary objective.
At least one treatment-emergent adverse event: 42.9% of treated versus 34.5% placebo participants in the stated efficacy-treatment period.
records.limitations: Different placebo run-in from FORWARD-4/5 SPCD. Publication and registry are not evidence of a downloaded complete protocol or SAP.
